newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Dec 10.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Dec 10.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Amid intense criticism of the arena, planned developments costing A$2 million have begun on the Sydney Cricket Ground surface. The SCG Trust may take two years to proceed with the project but has commenced with some major initial changes. Page 18.

Olympic silver medallists in yachting, Mitch Booth and Andrew Landenberger have announced they will part their ways for the Sydney Games. After an amicable separation, the pair will rejoin for a two-boat Tornado program in the next four years. The yachting couple were recently named 1996 Australian yachtsmen of the year. Page 18.

Superleague officials yesterday announced they would not be rushed into establishing a club in Melbourne. However, chief executive John Ribot said Superleague had always held plans for a team in Melbourne. Ribot was answering announcements made by the Ausralian Rugby League that the rebel competition planned to establish a team in time for the 1998 Optus Cup competition. Page 18.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Some bored spectators at Sunday night's match at the Sydney Cricket ground were arrested after they decided to provide their own entertainment on the ground. In what has been one of the worst matches in terms of disruptions, 12 people were apprehended for offensive conduct while others were detained for unlawful entry onto the playing field and alcohol-related offences. Page 42.

Some changes may be made to one-day cricket matches by the Australian Cricket Board. Following some criticism that the matches had incorporated 'unsporting' entertainment, some minor alterations may be introduced. Music will still be played at the fall of wickets but the theme will be to celebrate the bowler's achievement rather than humiliate the outgoing batsman. Page 42. --

Two of rugby union's greatest players are looking to move on in the sport. Australian player David Campese is seeking a contract with an English club while South African Francois Pienaar wants to play internationals for England. Page 42.
THE AGE

South Australian Collingwood recruit Johnathon Ross was sacked yesterday in a reaction to police charges on Ross and two other players last week. Aaron James and Trent Hotton have been fined by the club and will attend counselling in an attempt to improvetheir behaviour and alcohol control. Page C8.

Hawthorn has announced it would like to achieve 30,000 members within the next few years as a start towards building the club back up financially. The Australian Football League club's new board announced the changes in the wake of the failed merger withMelbourne. Page C8.

Tasmanian cricket captain David Boon has warned Victoria's stand-in skipper Dean Jones of a viscous attack on the team after the Bushrangers put up the shutters and trudged to a draw last night. Page C8.
THE HERALD SUN

Queensland batsman Andrew Symonds has been warned he will be risking his A$140,000 contract if he plays for Australia A against the West Indies. Symonds' English county side Gloucestershire told the cricketer he could not keep his A$70,000-a-year contract which has two years to run, if he enters the field on Friday night. Page 72.

Melbourne football club is set to announce a A$250,000 profit at tonight's general meeting. The announcement of a new office and social facility for the club is also on the cards. The Demons will also describe plans for a new summer training venue. Page 6.

Queensland batsman Martin Love has been sidelined for the rest of the season with a knee injury. Love will have a knee reconstruction after Christmas after a training mishap caused the damage on Saturday. Love is disappointed as he had hopes of playing inthe Ashes tour. Page 68.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

New South Wales Shadow Racing Minister Richard Bull has urged Premier Bob Carr to put a stop to the practice of rounding down winning TAB dividends. Carr announced before last year's State election that rounding down would go when he became Premier, but te controversial practice is still swelling Government coffers with over A$30 million a year because of the rule.

National Basketball League chairman Malcolm Speed has his sights set on the Australian Rugby League chairmanship. While the ARL is not giving any hints away at who might replace current chief executive John Quayle, Speed is tipped to be one of the three cndidates. Page 58.

Australia's top alpine skier Zali Steggall has finished in third place at the Europa Cup event. Clocking the fastest time of the competition on her second run, Steggall was supported by coach Helmut Spiegl who said she would continue to prove her ability.Page 58.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
